threads.body: [Documentation] This comment references the pre-move opentelemetry-api bridge class/package and implies the tracer still uses a reflective bridge. With this PR adding Context#getData bridging and moving opentelemetry-api-1.0 under `opentelemetryapi.v1_0`, the comment is now misleading/outdated.

The PR description says this change is about moving `opentelemetry-api-1.0` instrumentation under a `v1_0` subpackage, but this module also adds new Azure SDK behavior (`AzureContextInstrumentation`) and a new test to validate explicit parent context bridging. Please update the PR description (or split into a separate PR) so reviewers/release notes don’t miss the functional change.

replies.body: No code change needed for this one. Updated the PR description to document the Azure Core 1.53 explicit parent context bridging behavior.

threads.body: The parent-context key is hard-coded as "trace-context" even though Azure exposes it as `com.azure.core.util.tracing.Tracer.PARENT_TRACE_CONTEXT_KEY` (used in the test). Using the constant avoids drift if Azure changes the key value in a future release.

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/8ffdaedd83881c2798ec24dc7a803d50d9c624c7.

Switched the helper to use Azure's public `Tracer.PARENT_TRACE_CONTEXT_KEY` constant instead of a local `"trace-context"` literal.

threads.body: The Javadoc still refers to the parent-context entry as the hard-coded key "trace-context". Since Azure exposes this as the public constant `Tracer.PARENT_TRACE_CONTEXT_KEY` (and the helper now uses it), the Javadoc should reference the constant to avoid drift if Azure ever changes the key value.
